title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a scratch sheet. It is not about divided powers itself; it opens the thread continued on the next page: the canonical uniformization torsor of a curve of genus g >= 2, understood as a PGL(2) bundle with an integrable connection. In modern terms this is Gunning's indigenous bundle, i.e. a PGL2-oper.

(1) Top block: characteristic classes under isogeny. Grothendieck writes GP(1) for PGL(2).
- He sets up the central extensions 1 -> mu_2 -> SL(2,C) -> PGL(2,C) -> 1 and 1 -> mu_2 -> SL(2,R) -> PGL(2,R) -> 1.
- Maximal tori: T_C ~ G_m and the compact T^0_R = SO(2,R) ~ S^1.
- He compares characteristic classes along the squaring map on tori: 1/2 c_2^* = c'_2 and 1/2 E_1 = E'_1. Pulling back along the double cover multiplies the first Chern/Euler class by 2; equivalently classes of PGL2-bundles become half-integral once lifted.
- He makes SO(2) explicit as matrices (a b; -b a) with a^2+b^2 = 1. Since (a+ib)(a-ib) = 1, put lambda = a+ib and mu = a-ib with lambda mu = 1. Then a = (lambda+lambda^{-1})/2 and b = (lambda-lambda^{-1})/2i. This diagonalizes SO(2) over C to the split torus G_m.

(2) Middle/left: bundles on a curve X.
- 'Omega (x) Omega' signals that here Omega is a square root of the canonical bundle, a theta characteristic (Omega^{(x)2} = Omega^1_X).
- The PGL2-bundle is then P(Omega + Omega^{-1}) = P(K^{1/2} (+) K^{-1/2}).
- The non-split extension 0 -> Omega -> E -> Omega^{-1} -> 0 is classified by Ext^1(Omega^{-1}, Omega) = H^1(X, Omega^{(x)2}) = H^1(X, K) ~ C. Hence 'H^1(X,Omega) ~ C': up to scaling there is a unique non-split extension, the uniformizing (indigenous) rank-2 bundle.
- The section given by Omega in P(E) has normal bundle Omega^{-2} = T_X. This is Griffiths transversality / the oper condition.
- The gradeds 'Omega^2, Omega, O' and 'Omega^{-1} Omega^{-2} / Omega, O' are filtrations of the rank-3 adjoint / Sym^2 bundle and of the principal parts. This is the PGL2 = SO(3) picture, with gradeds K^{-1}, O, K, equivalently the jet bundle P^2 twisted.

(3) Right side: linear differential equations via principal parts.
- There are exact sequences 0 -> Sym^n Omega^1 -> P^n_{X/k} -> P^{n-1}_{X/k} -> 0.
- An n-th order operator is D: P^n_{X/k} -> L, i.e. the equation a_n f^{(n)} + ... + a_0 f = 0.
- A first-order equation Df + alpha f = 0 corresponds to a connection E -> E (x) Omega^1_{X/S}.
- An epimorphism E -> O_X with dual O_X -> E-check is noted. P^n is split as O_X + P^{n+}, the augmentation ideal part, which is where divided-power/PD-envelope considerations link to the rest of the cote.
- The problem served is the dictionary between n-th order linear ODEs with nondegenerate symbol and rank-n bundles with connection plus a full flag (opers). For n = 2 it specializes to projective structures, i.e. PGL2-bundles with connection and a transverse section.
- The next page applies this to the canonical uniformization torsor (from pi_1 -> PSL(2,R) ⊂ PGL(2,C)). It asks for a 'canonical algebraic integrable connection' on P(Omega^{-1}+Omega).
errors: b = (lambda - mu)/(2i), but the second expression 1/2(lambda - lambda^{-1}) drops the factor 1/i; it should be (lambda - lambda^{-1})/(2i).

Notational trap rather than an error: Omega on the left half means a square root of the canonical bundle (cf. 'Omega (x) Omega'). With Omega = Omega^1 literally, P(Omega + Omega^{-1}) would be the wrong ruled surface (section normal bundle K^{-2} instead of T_X).

Implicit gap: the uniformizing connection is canonical on each fixed curve but not algebraic in families (it depends real-analytically on moduli). The next page's request for an algebraic canonical connection can only be met fiberwise; on a single curve there is a whole affine space H^0(K^2) of algebraic projective structures, the Fuchsian one not being algebraically singled out.

ideas.what: Relation of characteristic classes under SL2 -> PGL2 and SO(2) double cover (factor 1/2 on c1/Euler classes)
ideas.modern_name: characteristic classes under central isogeny; Euler class of SO(2) vs PSO(2)

ideas.what: Unique non-split extension of K^{-1/2} by K^{1/2} classified by H^1(X,K) = C, giving the uniformizing PGL2-bundle P(K^{1/2}+K^{-1/2}) with integrable connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, 'Special coordinate coverings of Riemann surfaces'); opers: Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s); p-adic theory: Mochizuki (1996-99)

ideas.what: Linear differential operators as D: P^n_{X/k} -> L, with graded Sym^n Omega^1 and the link to connections
ideas.modern_name: differential operators via principal parts (EGA IV 16); ODE <-> oper dictionary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (EGA IV §16) for principal parts; ODE/connection dictionary classical (Deligne 1970 for the equivalence)
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16 (principal parts and differential operators)

ideas.what: Adjoint/rank-3 picture: gradeds K^{-1}, O, K for PGL2 = SO(3)-oper, related to twisted 2-jets
ideas.modern_name: Sym^2 of oper / sl2-oper adjoint filtration

missed.claim: In a 1975-76 dossier on the divided-power de Rham complex, Grothendieck formulates the uniformization of curves as a canonical PGL2-torsor with integrable connection (an indigenous bundle). He asks for an algebraic canonical connection on P(Omega^{-1}+Omega), where Omega is a theta characteristic, and juxtaposes it with principal parts P^n_{X/k} and PD structures. This is essentially the setting Mochizuki later developed into p-adic Teichmüller theory (indigenous bundles plus crystalline/PD methods), independently and about 20 years later. The record does not credit Grothendieck with considering indigenous bundles or their crystalline aspect.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's interest in the uniformization torsor and in opers in the context of crystalline/PD differential calculus, prefiguring Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory. The page itself contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard (Gunning's indigenous bundles, principal parts). The interest is historical: an unpublished Grothendieck engagement with the uniformization PGL2-oper next to the PD de Rham complex, prefiguring themes of Mochizuki and Beilinson–Drinfeld. Nothing finished or new is on the page.
transcription_corrections: b = (λ-μ)/(2i) is followed by Grothendieck's own 1/2(λ - λ^{-1}), which omits the i.
'Ω⊗Ω' likely signals that Ω denotes a square root of the canonical bundle on this page.
'P^3' near 'Ω^2 Ω O' may be a 'P' (principal parts/projective) with exponent rather than projective 3-space; uncertain.
'Ω^{n-1}_C' at top right is probably Ω^{n-1} or Ω^{n+1} over C, part of the principal-parts sequence; uncertain.
'(n) épi' refers to the map E → O_X being an epimorphism.
The final line '≃ O_X + P^{n+}_{X/k}' refers to the decomposition of P^n_{X/k} written vertically under P^n.
